evidence: Quick Design-only project/delivery review of specs/spec.md, design/design.md, and design/contract.json. Ownership, rollback feasibility, one-way-door handling, and the seven-leaf/shared-adapter shape are otherwise explicit, but the executable integration dependency contract is internally inconsistent.

findings.issue: The integration lane's machine-readable depends_on set omits AC2 even though its adjacent rule and design/design.md:228-234 require all seven leaf owners to be green, while it includes AC7 as a completed dependency even though AC7 validation requires the final integrated candidate and terminal adapters that this lane connects.
findings.why: This makes the delivery order non-executable: a consumer of depends_on can start shared integration before the Design-sweep leaf is ready, or deadlock waiting for AC7 completion that itself needs the shared integration. That dependency inversion invalidates the stated leaf-wave to integration to final-validation sequence.
findings.suggestion: Replace acceptance-id dependencies with explicit leaf-readiness receipts for all seven lanes (including AC2), let the integration lane depend on those receipts, and place AC7 end-to-end acceptance/finalization after the integration receipt; update the pair map and prose to use the same milestones.
